_doc: Methodology contract for the NFRI site. Rendered by harness/build_essays.py into <section id='methodology'>. Weights, λ values and gate logic are mirrored from contract/risk_model.json + contract/feature_dictionary.md — keep in sync if those change.

blocks.text: Acts I–IV argue that availability loss is mispriced because the market reads damage, not posture. Findings is the empirical pass: four predictions walked against the live slice. This section is the construct those predictions depend on: two axes, fused evidence, honest tiers. When registers refresh, ordering inside quadrants should move; the margin definition should not.

Every entity is scored on Exposure and Preparedness, each a weighted sum of five sub-factors on a 0–4 scale, rescaled to 0–100. Scoring is arithmetic in code, never a model's free-text opinion. Judgement enters only where a register cannot reach, fused with hard data under published credibility weights.

The axis score is E = (Σ wi · reff,i / 4) × 100 (and likewise P on the preparedness side): a weighted average of effective sub-factor ratings, where each reff fuses a register reading and a research reading (below). Margin of Safety is P − E: two axes before any single headline number. Median cut-lines on the live universe define the four quadrants (not fixed 50/50), so the field re-centres as the universe grows but the construct stays stable.

blocks.caption: Exposure axis — the size of the bet
head: Sub-factor
Weight
What it measures
rows: Book concentration
Share of premium / revenue in energy, property and data-centre / specialty classes.
Non-firm intensity
MW-weighted share of capacity on flexible / curtailable connections, or behind an un-progressed gate.
Aggregation / correlation
Herfindahl concentration of covered MW across grid supply points and constraint boundaries.{{cite:ACT-HHI-EIOPA}}
Trigger gap
Whether relevant cover relies on physical-damage triggers only, with no availability / parametric layer.{{cite:ACAD-TEH-WOOLNOUGH-TRIGGER,ACAD-LICHTENBERG-TRIGGER}}
Tenor mismatch
Cover / facility tenor versus the years of credible curtailment claims history.

blocks.caption: Preparedness axis — the ability to carry it
head: Sub-factor
Weight
What it measures
rows: Data & monitoring
Verifiable telemetry, datasets or audited monitoring of availability risk (no vendor self-claims).
Product fit
Count of distinct, evidenced non-damage / parametric products tied to power or data-centre risk.
Underwriting expertise
Named specialist function, evidenced via regulatory approvals or disclosed hires.
Capital & reinsurance
Financial-strength rating and Solvency II SCR-coverage, mapped to 0–4 by a fixed lookup.{{cite:PRA-SII-SCR,RATING-AMBEST-FSR}}
Pricing & modelling
Published or documented methodology for pricing availability / curtailment risk.

blocks.caption: Sub-factor weights within each axis (sum to 1.00).

blocks.text: Each sub-factor can carry two ratings: a deterministic rating derived in code from a register or filing, and a latent rating from sourced research judgement. The effective rating is a credibility-weighted blend{{cite:ACT-CREDIBILITY}}: reff = clamp[0,4]( λ·rdet + (1−λ)·rlat ), where λ is set by the evidence tier of the deterministic input. Measured registers dominate; an assessed sub-factor falls back entirely to the research prior. That is how today's outside-in judgement becomes tomorrow's measured score as register trails land.

blocks.caption: Credibility weight λ by evidence tier (lowered slightly when input confidence is medium / low)
head: Tier of deterministic input
λ
Effect
rows: Measured (register)
Score is the register, essentially. Research prior barely moves it.
Derived (computed from registers)
Mostly the computed value; small room for judgement.
Disclosed (filing / rating)
Filing-led, judgement at the margin.
Assessed (no measurement)
Falls back entirely to the sourced research rating.
blocks.note: λ = max(0, λ_tier + δ_confidence), with δ = 0 / −0.05 / −0.10 for high / medium / low confidence in the deterministic input.

blocks.text: How directly each number is evidenced

Every value carries a tier, and the tier is load-bearing: it sets λ and it is shown on the entity drill-down. The four tiers describe how directly a rating is evidenced, from a register read straight off to a research judgement made where no measurement reaches. A reader can follow any rating back to its source.

head: Tier
Meaning
Example
rows: Measured
Read directly from a primary register.
MW on a flexible connection in the DNO Embedded Capacity Register.
Disclosed
Stated in a filing, rating or regulatory record.
Financial-strength rating; Solvency II SCR coverage.
Derived
Computed deterministically from measured / disclosed inputs.
Herfindahl index over grid supply points.
Assessed
Sourced research judgement where no measurement exists.
Pricing capability, capped and confidence-limited.

blocks.text: Some sub-factors can be measured and others cannot: three Preparedness sub-factors (data & monitoring, underwriting expertise, pricing & modelling) rest on judgement by their nature, so the measurable load sits mostly on the Exposure axis, where non-firm intensity comes from the registers, book concentration from filings, and aggregation is derived from grid geography.

While live registers and filings are still being read across the universe, scores stay provisional until the publication gate clears at 60% blended measured/disclosed share (L5), currently {{fact:measured_pct}} on {{fact:total}} entities. What should move as tiers land is ordering inside quadrants. What should not move is the construct: two axes, one margin, and the four predictions Findings tests against the slice. Open any entity for its provenance trail, or see the Methodology page for the full gate and pipeline.
